title: 536–542 AD darkness and cooling linked to volcanism or comet debris
summary: Randall Carlson tells of 536–542 AD darkness and cooling linked to volcanism or comet debris, about 536-542 AD at Europe, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Uh the years 536 to 542 AD were periods where, you know, the the the the the records of the monks and the the people who were living through that time talk about weeks and months at a time when they couldn't see the sun.

plain: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient catastrophes, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that from 536 to 542 AD, records left by monks and others in Europe describe weeks and months when they could not see the sun. He ties this darkness and cooling to either volcanic eruptions or debris from a comet, an idea he links to the astronomer Fred Hoyle. If true, it would show how something from space could darken the whole sky within recorded history.
